title: Flow plan
description: Which stages this one ticket actually needs. Written by the Router — a script when a deterministic rule matches, a cheap model when none does — and read by every hand-off after it.

reasoning.description: One to three sentences: why this kind and why this route. What a human reads when they disagree with it.

risk.description: How expensive it would be to get this wrong. High risk routes to a human whatever the rest of this says.

route.description: Ordered. An empty route means the Router will not decide this one, which sends it to a human rather than guessing.

gates.description: ADDITIVE ONLY. A gate the config has on stays on whatever this says; the Router may ask for a gate the config does not require, never waive one it does. Routing around a human gate is the one thing a routing decision must not be able to do.

on_complete.description: merge: the ordinary end. file-issue-only: an audit, which has no PR and turns every finding into its own issue. comment-only: a question or a spike, answered in writing and deliberately not built.

confidence.description: How sure the Router is of this route. Below gates.min_route_confidence the issue goes to a human, and an absent score counts as below.

matched_rule.description: Set when a deterministic rule decided this and no model ran. 'Matched by script' has to be visible, not silent.

route_request.description: A later stage asking the Router to change the route mid-flight. Only the Router may grant it, and only against the graph.
